top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only configuration on the slate, and I judge it on literary merit, not on the six aligned round-1 preferences, which may reflect correlated reasoning from shared public knowledge. On public knowledge of Blinding and Solenoid, his voice is distinctive, his formal ambition is large and controlled, and memory, the body and dream are built into long architectures that read as a sustained metaphysical project rather than ornament. The citation scope I support is the narrowed one: centred on the Romanian novel, with poetry as lyric base and not a named achievement, because translation coverage of the poetry and early work is thin. I accept the peaks-and-overall-direction standard for a whole-oeuvre prize, on the condition that the peaks are several and the later work does not merely restate them. Whether Solenoid reorganises the architecture of the earlier trilogy or only restates it remains unresolved. No member has offered close reading, and I cannot judge Romanian syntax, rhythm or register directly. That uncertainty argues for caution in the citation wording, not for withholding the award, since no award (P000) would rest on a doubt the record does not substantiate. I therefore rank P001 first and P000 second. I have not independently verified sources or read the full corpus of any candidate.
